edges.description: CST1A and CST1B are antagonistic community state types, so depleting CST1A directly releases CST1B from competition.
Achromobacter spanius is a CST1A-derived taxon, so the same community shift that establishes CST1B dominance removes it.
edges.target: Loss of Achromobacter spanius Mucosal Protection

edges.description: Loss of the protective CST1A taxon aggravates gastric mucosal injury. The protective direction is established in animal and cell-culture models; the intermediates linking it to human ulceration are not resolved.
edges.source: Loss of Achromobacter spanius Mucosal Protection
edges.target: H. pylori and NSAID-associated mucosal injury

nodes.description: Depletion of CST1A allows pathogenic CST1B communities to dominate the gastric microbiota. CST1B is enriched in gastroduodenal disease and favors nucleotide and peptidoglycan biosynthesis pathways. The CST1A-CST1B imbalance is preserved across age cohorts and disease stages. Note the provenance of that claim: the core structure was defined in a discovery cohort of 255 pediatric samples, and its persistence across disease stages rests on cross-cohort validation over eight further datasets (n = 1,299), not on the primary cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Core gastric microbiota linked to pathogenesis and preserved across age-stratified cohorts.
evidence.snippet: CST1A is enriched in non-ulcer controls, whereas CST1B is associated with gastroduodenal disease

evidence.snippet: Peptic ulcers not associated with H pylori infection or the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are now also imposing substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.

nodes.description: H. pylori infection selectively depletes CST1A bacterial taxa from the gastric microbiota. CST1A communities are enriched in non-ulcer controls and linked to protective motility-related processes; their depletion is the primary microbiota-disrupting effect of H. pylori.

nodes.description: Depletion of CST1A taxa eliminates CST1A-derived Achromobacter spanius, which normally alleviates gastric mucosal injury through anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Loss of this protective commensal removes a key mucosal safeguard and contributes to ulceration.
nodes.id: Loss of Achromobacter spanius Mucosal Protection
